static_traits.name: Lin Rui
static_traits.family_status: Lives with parents and a younger brother; family is supportive, but the client finds it hard to express the 'sense of failure' to them
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends, but finds it hard to open up to friends about feelings of failure
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no psychotherapy history; no similar psychological problem history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, high cooperativeness, positive attitude; tending to use exaggerated and dichotomous expressions (like 'I will never be independent' / 'I have always been a failure'); self-critical and comparative tendency; limited expression in intimate relationships

basic_info.main_problem: I feel I am a failure in life, because I still live with my parents, and this thought affects my self-esteem and my view of the future.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because this sense of failure is affecting my self-esteem and happiness, and I hope to deal with it before it escalates further.

special_situations.event: Sees peers posting updates on social media about independent living (renting their own place / having their own home)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I still live with my parents at 25, it means I am behind, a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Relieving thoughts by distracting attention with soccer, painting, and reading
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them, I have fallen behind

special_situations.event: Casual chats with classmates or friends involve living situations and independent living
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Failing to meet society's independence expectations for peers proves I am not good enough, and others will look down on me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding discussing his feelings deeply, not opening up to family or friends to avoid worrying them
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am not independent enough, I cannot do it

special_situations.event: Noticing he still lives with his parents (returning home or thinking of living arrangements)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Success and failure are divided by whether one lives independently; not being independent equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-criticism, constantly thinking about 'how to prove he can be independent'

special_situations.event: When seeing peers who are more independent, compares with her own academic achievements
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only living independently counts as truly valuable; other achievements do not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring existing strengths and achievements, focusing attention on inadequacies

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen as an independent, valuable adult and gain recognition
core_conflict.fear: Worries about being judged a failure by others; feels shame and being misunderstood
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of security by reducing self-disclosure (not talking deeply with family)
Uses self-criticism and comparison to push oneself to change

object_relations.object_representation: Peers / society experienced as judges and a superior standard

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others raise topics of living independence or comparing with peers
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client tends to think he will be judged or misunderstood; exposing vulnerability equals not being understood
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tending to give reasons like 'do not want to worry them' in a tactful, cautious tone, avoiding deep emotional details; using factual statements, fewer emotional words.

manifestations: Directly equating life success with whether one lives independently
Holding a negative outlook on the future (feeling he will always fail)
Finds it hard to open up to family and friends about feelings of failure
Choosing not to express for fear of being misunderstood

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Views society's expectation of independence for peers as a standard that must be obeyed ('I should already be independent')
Directly using living status as the basis for judging self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently self-labeling as 'a failure', using extreme language to judge himself
Overly cautious when communicating with family, not expressing true feelings for fear of worrying them

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: When feelings of failure rise, turns to soccer, painting, and reading to distract himself
Tending to downplay or deflect the topic when living arrangements come up

positive_force: Good academic performance, able to manage heavy course load
Willing to seek professional help, positive attitude
negative_force: Excessive comparison and external standard dependence (external validation)
Cognitive biases such as black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, mental filtering
Expression limited; hard to share feelings with close people

target_behavior.behavior: Compares daily and labels self a 'failure'
antecedent: Sees friends' independent-living posts on social media
Discusses housing and independence topics with classmates/friends
Being at parents' home or thinking he still lives with his parents
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjecting society's value conditions on peer independence, directly equating living situation with self-worth, viewing success and failure in black-and-white terms
target_behavior.function: Attempts through self-criticism to push himself to change and become independent quickly (superficial self-motivation), while avoiding acknowledging complex realities and emotions
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood and decreased drive, interest activities affected, impaired self-esteem

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding expressing failure feelings to family and friends
antecedent: Thinking about discussing one's feelings with family
When asked about housing or independence topics in conversation
target_behavior.core_reason: Worried about worrying family, being misunderstood or judged, thus repressing vulnerability and shame
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential negative evaluation and uncomfortable emotions, maintaining short-term psychological security
target_behavior.consequence: Increased loneliness, decreased opportunities to receive support, persistent negative thinking
